fields.why: Seven self-identified race/ethnicity groups each get an adjusted prevalence and an APR against White adults (Table), an outcome measured in each of 3 or more SPD groups.

Race/ethnicity drives the Table. Age, education and income are ordered SPDs with claims that prevalence 'differed' and 'generally decreased' across their levels; sex is a pair, and region and self-rated health are not SPDs.

The methods make CI overlap ('any two estimates') the only significance criterion, so the 'most prevalent among' race claims and the 'differed by' age/education/income claims rest on it. Under the brief's blanket-method rule that makes them per-group vs referent only, not side by side; the APR entry already is.

brief_issues: Section F says outright only for a blanket t-test that a method stated once, under 'highest/higher' claims, gives per-group vs referent only. It could say the same for a stated CI-overlap rule, so readers stop recording those claims as side by side while also listing a CI overlap assertion procedure. The age/SES entry is the closest call, since its estimates are only in the supplement.
